thesis: Technical autonomy consists in rule-bound self-selection of admissible continuations, not independence from an environment.
reasons: Every operation depends on prior state and declared constraints.
Environmental input does not directly determine stabilization.
objections: Calling constrained execution autonomous may stretch the ordinary meaning of autonomy.
responses: The thesis explicitly qualifies autonomy as technical and operational rather than absolute or metaphysical.
sources: Recursive Codex architecture and stabilized events
